symptom: PC on VLAN 10 cannot reach PC on VLAN 10 connected to a different switch
show_output:
Switch# show vlan brief
VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
10   Sales                            active    Fa0/1, Fa0/2
20   Engineering                      active    Fa0/3, Fa0/4
root_cause: Access port on the second switch is assigned to VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10, causing a VLAN mismatch across the link
fix: Reassign the access port to VLAN 10 with 'switchport access vlan 10' and verify with 'show vlan brief'

symptom: Devices on a trunk link intermittently lose connectivity and CDP native VLAN mismatch warnings appear in the log
show_output:
Switch# show interfaces trunk
Port        Mode         Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gi0/1       on           802.1q         trunking      1
%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet0/1 (1), with SwitchB GigabitEthernet0/1 (99)
root_cause: The native VLAN configured on Gi0/1 is VLAN 1 on this switch but VLAN 99 on the neighboring switch
fix: Set matching native VLANs on both ends with 'switchport trunk native vlan 99' and confirm consistency

symptom: Trunk port between two switches is not passing tagged traffic for any VLAN
show_output:
Switch# show interfaces gigabitEthernet0/1 switchport
Name: Gi0/1
Switchport: Enabled
Administrative Mode: trunk
Operational Mode: static access
Trunking Encapsulation: Negotiate
root_cause: The trunk failed to negotiate 802.1q encapsulation because the switch model requires it to be set explicitly with 'switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q' before trunk mode is applied
fix: Configure 'switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q' then 'switchport mode trunk' on Gi0/1

symptom: New laptops joining the Sales VLAN fail to receive an IP address while existing devices keep working
show_output:
Router# show ip dhcp pool SALES_POOL
Pool SALES_POOL :
 Utilization mark (high/low)    : 100 / 0
 Total addresses                : 254
 Leased addresses               : 254
 Excluded addresses             : 3
 Pending event                  : none
root_cause: The DHCP pool for the Sales VLAN is fully leased out, exhausting all available addresses
fix: Expand the pool's network/prefix, shorten the lease duration, or add a secondary DHCP scope; verify with 'show ip dhcp pool SALES_POOL'

symptom: Clients on VLAN 30 are receiving IP addresses from the VLAN 20 subnet and cannot communicate locally
show_output:
Router# show running-config | section dhcp
ip dhcp pool VLAN30_POOL
 network 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.30.1
root_cause: The DHCP pool intended for VLAN 30 was configured with the VLAN 20 network range, handing out mismatched addresses
fix: Correct the 'network' statement in VLAN30_POOL to 192.168.30.0 255.255.255.0 and restart the DHCP service

symptom: All hosts on a subnet can reach local devices but cannot reach the internet or other VLANs
root_cause: The default gateway configured on the host (192.168.1.1) is not on the same subnet as the host's IP address, so gateway traffic cannot be delivered
fix: Correct the default gateway to 192.168.10.1 (the router subinterface for that VLAN) via DHCP scope or static config

symptom: Two PCs on the same VLAN report intermittent connectivity loss and an IP conflict warning appears
show_output:
PC> ipconfig /all
An error occurred while renewing interface Local Area Connection : IP address conflict detected on 192.168.10.20 with MAC 0060.2F8B.0912
root_cause: Two devices were statically assigned the same IP address (192.168.10.20), causing an address conflict on the LAN
fix: Reassign one device to a unique IP address outside the DHCP pool range or convert it to DHCP; verify with 'show ip dhcp binding'

symptom: A workstation configured with a static IP cannot communicate with any device outside its own /30-sized view of the network
root_cause: The subnet mask (/30) is far too small for the intended /24 network, causing the host to believe most of the subnet, including its gateway, is unreachable
fix: Correct the subnet mask to 255.255.255.0 to match the VLAN's addressing plan

symptom: Branch router can ping directly connected networks but cannot reach the head-office network across the WAN link
show_output:
Router# show ip route
Gateway of last resort is not set
     192.168.10.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
     10.0.0.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0
root_cause: No static or default route exists pointing toward the head-office network (172.16.0.0/16) or the WAN next hop
fix: Add a static route 'ip route 172.16.0.0 255.255.0.0 10.0.0.2' or configure 'ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 10.0.0.2' as a default route

symptom: Remote administrator cannot establish an SSH session to a router even though the service is enabled and reachable by ping
show_output:
Router# show access-lists
Extended IP access list BLOCK_MGMT
    10 deny tcp any any eq 22
    20 permit ip any any
Router# show run | include access-class
line vty 0 4
 access-class BLOCK_MGMT in
root_cause: Access-list BLOCK_MGMT explicitly denies TCP port 22 (SSH) and is applied inbound on the VTY lines
fix: Add a permit entry above the deny for the management subnet, e.g. 'permit tcp 192.168.100.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 22', or remove the deny 22 line

symptom: Users cannot open internal web application over HTTP even though the server responds to ping
show_output:
Router# show access-lists WEB_FILTER
Extended IP access list WEB_FILTER
    10 deny tcp any any eq 80
    20 permit ip any any
root_cause: Access-list WEB_FILTER blocks TCP port 80 (HTTP) traffic destined to the server, applied on the router interface facing the clients
fix: Modify ACL to permit TCP port 80 to the server's address specifically, or remove the blanket deny statement

symptom: Telnet access to a switch from the management VLAN fails with connection refused / timed out
show_output:
Switch# show access-lists
Standard IP access list 10
    10 deny   192.168.99.0, wildcard bits 0.0.0.255
    20 permit any
Switch# show run | include access-class
line vty 0 15
 access-class 10 in
root_cause: ACL 10 denies the entire management subnet 192.168.99.0/24 from Telnet access on the VTY lines
fix: Update ACL 10 to permit the management subnet or add a specific permit statement above the deny, then reapply

symptom: Internal hosts behind NAT cannot reach the internet even though the ISP link is up and routing is correct
show_output:
Router# show ip nat translations
Router# show ip nat statistics
Total active translations: 0 (0 static, 0 dynamic; 0 extended)
Peak translations: 0
root_cause: No NAT translations are being created because the inside/outside interface roles were never designated with 'ip nat inside'/'ip nat outside'
fix: Apply 'ip nat inside' on the LAN-facing interface and 'ip nat outside' on the WAN-facing interface, then verify with 'show ip nat translations'

symptom: Only a handful of internal hosts can reach the internet at a time; others get connection timeouts during business hours
show_output:
Router# show ip nat statistics
Total active translations: 253 (0 static, 253 dynamic; 0 extended)
Hits: 91820  Misses: 4021
Pool NAT_POOL: netmask 255.255.255.248
 start 203.0.113.1 end 203.0.113.6
 total addresses 6, allocated 6 (100%), misses 4021
root_cause: The NAT address pool (only 6 public addresses) is exhausted under normal load, causing PAT/NAT overload failures for additional hosts
fix: Expand the NAT pool size or convert to a single-address 'ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/0 overload' configuration

symptom: A branch office reports total loss of internet access after a small config change; NAT stopped translating any traffic
show_output:
Router# show run | section nat
ip nat inside source list 1 pool NAT_POOL overload
!
access-list 1 deny any
root_cause: The NAT source access-list (ACL 1) was mistakenly configured to deny all traffic instead of permitting the inside network, so nothing matches for translation
fix: Change 'access-list 1 deny any' to 'access-list 1 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255' to correctly match inside hosts for NAT

symptom: A redundant link between two switches has been disabled by Spanning Tree, and users complain of reduced bandwidth
show_output:
Switch# show spanning-tree
VLAN0010
  Spanning tree enabled protocol ieee
Interface           Role Sts Cost      Prio.Nbr Type
-------------------- ---- --- --------- -------- --------
Gi0/1                Root FWD 4         128.1    P2p
Gi0/2                Altn BLK 4         128.2    P2p
root_cause: Spanning Tree Protocol has correctly placed Gi0/2 into blocking state to prevent a Layer 2 loop, which is expected behavior on a redundant topology without EtherChannel
fix: This is normal STP behavior; if more bandwidth is desired, configure EtherChannel (LACP) across both links to bundle them instead of relying on a blocked redundant path

symptom: A user's PC was accidentally connected into a hub creating a switching loop, and now the whole floor loses connectivity intermittently
show_output:
Switch# show spanning-tree summary
Root bridge for: none
Extended system ID enabled
%SPANTREE-2-LOOPGUARD_BLOCK: Loop guard blocking port Fa0/5 on VLAN0010
root_cause: A Layer 2 loop was introduced when a hub/switch was cross-connected, but Loop Guard correctly blocked the offending port before a broadcast storm could form
fix: Remove the improperly cross-connected cable creating the loop, then verify the port using 'shutdown' / 'no shutdown' to clear the Loop Guard block

symptom: An access port connected to an end-user PC transitioned to err-disabled after the PC was rebooted with a hub attached
show_output:
Switch# show interfaces status err-disabled
Port      Name               Status       Reason
Fa0/8                        err-disabled  bpduguard
%PM-4-ERR_DISABLE: bpduguard error detected on Fa0/8, putting Fa0/8 in err-disable state
root_cause: PortFast was enabled on Fa0/8 without disabling BPDU Guard, and the port received a BPDU (from the hub-connected device or loop), tripping BPDU Guard and disabling the port
fix: Remove the offending loop/device, then recover the port with 'shutdown' followed by 'no shutdown', or enable 'errdisable recovery cause bpduguard'

symptom: All hosts on a subnet can reach IP addresses directly but cannot browse to any websites by name
show_output:
PC> nslookup www.cisco.com
DNS request timed out.
   timeout was 2 seconds.
*** Request to UnKnown timed out
PC> ping 8.8.8.8
Reply from 8.8.8.8: bytes=32 time=10ms TTL=128
root_cause: The configured DNS server address is unreachable from the client subnet, so name resolution requests never receive a response even though internet routing works
fix: Verify the DNS server is reachable, correct the DNS server IP in the DHCP scope or client config, and confirm with 'nslookup'

symptom: Users report that www.internal.corp resolves to the wrong server and loads an outdated website
show_output:
Server# show dns-server host-entries
www.internal.corp    A     192.168.1.50   (should be 192.168.1.150)
root_cause: An incorrect/stale A record maps www.internal.corp to the old server's address instead of the current web server
fix: "Update the DNS host entry to point www.internal.corp to 192.168.1.150 and clear client DNS caches"

symptom: A laptop cannot find the office wireless network in its available networks list
show_output:
AccessPoint# show running-config | section ssid
interface Dot11Radio0
 ssid CorpWiFi-Secure
Client radio configured SSID: CorpNet-Secure
root_cause: The SSID configured on the client (CorpNet-Secure) does not match the access point's broadcast SSID (CorpWiFi-Secure)
fix: Reconfigure the client to connect using the correct SSID 'CorpWiFi-Secure', or rename the AP SSID to match documented standards

symptom: A laptop can see the wireless network but repeatedly fails to authenticate and never gets an IP address
show_output:
AccessPoint# show running-config | section encryption
interface Dot11Radio0
 encryption mode ciphers aes-ccm
 authentication key-management wpa version 2
Client: WPA2-PSK passphrase mismatch, association failed
root_cause: The client's WPA2 pre-shared key does not match the passphrase configured on the access point, causing authentication to fail before an IP can be assigned
fix: Correct the WPA2 passphrase on the client to match the AP's configured key, then reconnect and verify DHCP lease is obtained

symptom: A newly cabled server has no link light and cannot be reached at all from the network
show_output:
Switch# show interfaces GigabitEthernet0/5
GigabitEthernet0/5 is administratively down, line protocol is down
  Full-duplex, 1000Mb/s, media type is 10/100/1000BaseTX
root_cause: The interface was left administratively shut down (likely from a prior configuration or accidental 'shutdown' command), so no link can form regardless of cabling
fix: Issue 'no shutdown' on GigabitEthernet0/5 and verify link status changes to 'up, line protocol is up'

symptom: A workstation was moved to a new port and immediately lost network access; the port shows a security violation
show_output:
Switch# show port-security interface FastEthernet0/6
Port Security              : Enabled
Port Status                : Secure-shutdown
Violation Mode              : Shutdown
Maximum MAC Addresses       : 1
Total MAC Addresses         : 1
Last Source Address:Vlan   : 00E0.8F1A.5C3B:10
root_cause: Port security on Fa0/6 was configured with a sticky/static MAC address for the previous device; the new workstation's differing MAC address triggered a security violation and shut the port down
fix: Clear the port-security violation with 'shutdown' / 'no shutdown' and either clear the sticky MAC or reconfigure with the correct address, or raise 'maximum' if multiple devices are expected

symptom: A new VLAN was assigned to several ports but end devices on those ports cannot communicate with anything, even each other
show_output:
Switch# show vlan brief
VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
1    default                          active
Switch# show interfaces Fa0/9 switchport
Administrative Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 40 (Inactive)
root_cause: VLAN 40 was assigned to interface Fa0/9 but was never created in the switch's VLAN database, leaving the port in an inactive VLAN state
fix: Create the VLAN with 'vlan 40' / 'name <name>' in global config, then verify the port becomes active in 'show vlan brief'

symptom: A router with subinterfaces for inter-VLAN routing is not routing traffic for VLAN 50 even though the physical trunk is up
show_output:
Router# show ip interface brief
GigabitEthernet0/0.50     unassigned      YES manual administratively down down
Router# show run interface gigabitEthernet0/0.50
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.50
 encapsulation dot1Q 500
 ip address 192.168.50.1 255.255.255.0
root_cause: The subinterface was configured with 'encapsulation dot1Q 500' instead of the correct VLAN tag 50, so it never matches frames tagged for VLAN 50 arriving on the trunk
fix: Correct the encapsulation statement to 'encapsulation dot1Q 50' matching the actual VLAN ID, then bring the subinterface up with 'no shutdown'

symptom: Two neighboring routers running OSPF never form a neighbor relationship even though the link is up and IPs are reachable
show_output:
Router# show ip ospf neighbor
Router# show ip ospf interface GigabitEthernet0/0
GigabitEthernet0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  Internet Address 10.0.0.1/30, Area 0
%OSPF: Mismatch Area ID for interface GigabitEthernet0/0 - local Area 0, remote Area 1
root_cause: The two routers have their OSPF interfaces configured in different areas (Area 0 vs Area 1), preventing a neighbor adjacency from forming
fix: Correct the network statement or interface area assignment so both routers use the same OSPF area, e.g. 'network 10.0.0.0 0.0.0.3 area 0' on both sides

symptom: OSPF neighbors flap up and down repeatedly (2-Way to Down) on a point-to-point WAN link
show_output:
Router# show ip ospf interface Serial0/0/0
  Hello interval 10, Dead interval 40
%OSPF-5-ADJCHG: Process 1, Nbr 10.0.0.2 on Serial0/0/0 from FULL to DOWN, Neighbor Down: Dead timer expired
(Remote router configured with Hello 5 / Dead 20)
root_cause: Mismatched OSPF hello and dead timers between the two routers cause the dead timer to expire before hello packets are received, flapping the adjacency
fix: Set matching hello/dead timers on both routers with 'ip ospf hello-interval 10' and 'ip ospf dead-interval 40' (or restore to matching defaults)

symptom: Two EIGRP routers on the same link never establish a neighbor relationship despite correct IP addressing
show_output:
Router# show ip eigrp neighbors
Router# debug eigrp packets
EIGRP: Received packet with AS 200, expected AS 100, discarding
root_cause: The routers are configured with mismatched EIGRP autonomous system numbers (AS 100 vs AS 200), causing all EIGRP packets to be discarded as unrecognized
fix: Reconfigure both routers to use the same EIGRP AS number, e.g. 'router eigrp 100' on both, matching the network design

symptom: An ACL intended to permit only the 192.168.10.0/24 subnet is unexpectedly permitting nearly the entire network range
show_output:
Router# show access-lists 20
Standard IP access list 20
    10 permit 192.168.10.0, wildcard bits 0.0.255.255
root_cause: The wildcard mask 0.0.255.255 was used instead of 0.0.0.255, matching any address in 192.168.0.0/16 rather than just the intended /24 subnet
fix: Correct the wildcard mask to 0.0.0.255 so the ACL matches only 192.168.10.0/24, then re-verify allowed traffic

symptom: When the active HSRP router is rebooted for maintenance, hosts lose their gateway and cannot fail over to the standby router
show_output:
Router# show standby brief
Interface   Grp Pri P State    Active          Standby         Virtual IP
Gi0/0       1   100  Active   local           unknown         192.168.1.1
(Standby router)  Router2# show standby brief
Interface   Grp Pri P State    Active          Standby         Virtual IP
Gi0/0       2   90   Active   local           unknown         192.168.1.2
root_cause: The two routers were configured with different HSRP group numbers (1 vs 2) and different virtual IP addresses, so they never recognize each other as part of the same standby group
fix: Configure both routers with the same HSRP group number and identical virtual IP address, e.g. 'standby 1 ip 192.168.1.1' on both

symptom: After adding a new switch to the network, VLANs configured elsewhere in the campus disappear from all switches
show_output:
Switch# show vtp status
VTP Version                    : 2
Configuration Revision         : 25
VTP Operating Mode             : Server
VTP Domain Name                : (blank on new switch, overriding higher revision)
root_cause: A newly added switch joined the VTP domain with a higher configuration revision number but an empty/incorrect VLAN database, propagating a VLAN wipe to the whole domain
fix: Reset the offending switch's VTP revision number (e.g. by changing domain name) before joining the domain, and restore the VLAN database from a backup switch

symptom: Large file transfers between two routers across a WAN link stall or fragment excessively while small packets work fine
show_output:
Router# show interfaces Serial0/0/0
Serial0/0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  MTU 1500 bytes
Remote Router# show interfaces Serial0/0/0
Serial0/0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  MTU 1400 bytes
root_cause: The two ends of the WAN link are configured with mismatched MTU values (1500 vs 1400), causing fragmentation and performance issues for larger packets
fix: Set matching MTU values on both ends of the link with 'mtu 1500' (or an agreed value), then verify with 'show interfaces'

symptom: A link between a switch and a server shows extremely high late collisions and poor throughput
show_output:
Switch# show interfaces FastEthernet0/12
FastEthernet0/12 is up, line protocol is up
  Half-duplex, 100Mb/s
  5000 late collisions, 12 output errors
Server NIC configured for: Full-duplex, 100Mb/s
root_cause: A duplex mismatch exists between the switch port (half-duplex) and the server NIC (full-duplex), producing late collisions and degraded performance
fix: Set both ends to full-duplex explicitly with 'duplex full' on the switchport, or ensure autonegotiation is enabled on both sides

symptom: DHCP clients on a subnet across a router hop from the DHCP server never receive an IP address, while clients on the DHCP server's own subnet work fine
show_output:
Router# show run interface GigabitEthernet0/1
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
 (no ip helper-address configured)
root_cause: The router interface facing the remote subnet lacks an 'ip helper-address' statement, so DHCP broadcast requests from that subnet are never relayed to the DHCP server
fix: Add 'ip helper-address 192.168.1.10' (the DHCP server's address) on GigabitEthernet0/1 to relay DHCP broadcasts

symptom: A busy NAT router starts denying new outbound connections for all users during peak hours despite having plenty of public IPs in the pool
show_output:
Router# show ip nat statistics
Total active translations: 5000 (0 static, 5000 dynamic; 0 extended)
%NAT-4-TRANSLATION_TABLE_FULL: NAT translation table for pool NAT_POOL is full
root_cause: The NAT translation table reached its maximum entry limit under high session volume, causing new outbound connection attempts to be dropped
fix: Increase the NAT translation table limit with 'ip nat translation max-entries' or shorten idle-timeout values with 'ip nat translation timeout', then monitor with 'show ip nat statistics'

symptom: A newly installed router interface shows correct IP configuration but line protocol never comes up and no traffic passes
show_output:
Router# show ip interface brief
GigabitEthernet0/0     192.168.1.1     YES manual administratively down down
root_cause: The interface remains administratively shut down because 'no shutdown' was never issued after initial configuration
fix: Issue 'no shutdown' on GigabitEthernet0/0 and confirm status changes to 'up, line protocol is up'

symptom: Traffic on a trunk link is dropped for one specific VLAN while all other VLANs pass normally between two switches
show_output:
Switch# show interfaces trunk
Port        Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/1       1-9,11-4094
Port        Vlans allowed and active in management domain
Gi0/1       1,10,20,30
root_cause: VLAN 10 is missing from the trunk's allowed VLAN list (the range excludes VLAN 10 by way of '1-9,11-4094'), so tagged frames for VLAN 10 are dropped on the trunk
fix: Add VLAN 10 back to the trunk's allowed list with 'switchport trunk allowed vlan add 10' on the Gi0/1 interface
